exam.title: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: Generative AI LLMs
exam.study_prerequisites: NVIDIA lists basic generative-AI and LLM understanding. Build lifecycle evidence across ML and transformer foundations, Python application contracts, prompting and RAG, controlled experimentation, data analysis and visualization, deployment, monitoring, and trustworthy-AI controls using synthetic or licensed data.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Core Machine Learning and AI Knowledge (30%)

review.notes: All five live weighted domains are mapped through a governed lifecycle from use case and data through model/adaptation/retrieval choice, implementation, controlled experiment, deployment, monitoring and trustworthy-AI evidence. Three scenarios, eight labs and 40 checks are included. Seven URLs are reachable and Udemy is automation-blocked; none are broken. The certification page's conflicting 50 and 50–60 question statements are preserved rather than reconciled by inference. No recalled/live item, dump or copied course content is used.

sources.title: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: Generative AI LLMs
sources.notes: Canonical five-domain weighted blueprint, prerequisite, delivery, price and two-year validity baseline; the page says both 50 questions and 50–60 questions, so the guide preserves the discrepancy.

sources.title: Getting Started With Deep Learning
sources.notes: Official eight-hour, USD 90 mapped neural-network and deep-learning foundation course; verify price and access at enrollment.

sources.title: Accelerating End-to-End Data Science Workflows
sources.notes: Official eight-hour, USD 90 RAPIDS data preparation, analysis, modeling and deployment course; verify price and access at enrollment.

sources.title: Introduction to Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing
sources.notes: Official six-hour, USD 30 mapped transformer course; direct endpoint displayed a maintenance/move notice when checked, so enter through the certification page and verify availability.

sources.title: Building LLM Applications With Prompt Engineering
sources.notes: Official eight-hour, USD 90 prompt and LLM-application course mapped on the certification page; extend it with explicit evaluation, injection and production-control evidence.

sources.title: Rapid Application Development With Large Language Models
sources.notes: Official eight-hour, USD 90 mapped course for encoder/decoder, orchestration and application experimentation; verify price and access at enrollment.

sources.title: NVIDIA Trustworthy AI
sources.notes: First-party privacy, safety/security, transparency and nondiscrimination principles plus model-card and guardrail context; translate principles into testable system controls.

sources.title: NCA-GENL NVIDIA Certified Generative AI LLMs Specialization
sources.notes: One-hour-48-minute course updated March 2026. It is too short to establish applied readiness alone; verify claims against first-party material and build the guide labs.

public_objective_groups.title: Core Machine Learning and AI Knowledge
public_objective_groups.description: Knowledge of algorithms, conventions, and techniques that allow computers to learn from and make predictions or decisions based on data.
objectives: Assist in deployment and evaluation of model scalability, performance, and reliability under the supervision of senior team members.
Awareness of the process of extracting insights from large datasets using data mining, data visualization, and similar techniques.
Build LLM use cases such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), chatbots, and summarizers.
Curate and embed content datasets for RAGs.
Familiarity with the fundamentals of machine learning (e.g., feature engineering, model comparison, cross validation).
Familiarity with the capabilities of Python natural language packages (spaCy, NumPy, vector databases, etc.).
Read research papers (articles, conference papers, etc.) to identify emerging LLM trends and technologies.
Select and use models to create text embeddings.
Use prompt engineering principles to create prompts to achieve desired results.
Use Python packages (spaCy, NumPy, Keras, etc.) to implement specific traditional machine learning analyses.

public_objective_groups.title: Data Analysis
public_objective_groups.description: Inspecting, cleansing, transforming, and modeling data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions, and supporting decision-making.
objectives: Awareness of the process of extracting insights from large datasets using data mining, data visualization, and similar techniques.
Compare models using statistical performance metrics, such as loss functions or proportion of explained variance.
Conduct data analysis under the supervision of a senior team member.
Create graphs, charts, or other visualizations to convey the results of data analysis using specialized software.
Identify relationships and trends or any factors that could affect the results of research.

public_objective_groups.title: Experimentation
public_objective_groups.description: Perform, evaluate, and interpret experiments, including AI model evaluation and the use of human subjects in labeling or reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
objectives: Assist in model training and training optimization under the supervision of a senior team member.
Assist in preparing (e.g., scraping, tokenization) large datasets for pretraining, fine-tuning, and RLHF.
Assist in the design and conduct of hardware or software tests for LLM applications.
Assist in the evaluation of current or emerging technologies to consider factors such as cost, portability, compatibility, or usability.
Awareness of, and/or participation in, data collection from human subjects (e.g., RLHF).
Evaluate and refine existing models / benchmarking.
Executes experimentation to evaluate models and pipelines.

public_objective_groups.title: Software Development
objectives: Assist in the deployment and evaluations of model scalability, performance, and reliability under the supervision of a senior team member.
Build LLM use cases such as RAGs, chatbots, and summarizers.
Familiarity with the capabilities of Python natural language packages (spaCy, NumPy, vector databases, etc.).
Identify system data, hardware, or software components required to meet user needs.
Monitor functioning of data collection, experiments, and other software processes.
Use Python packages (spaCy, NumPy, Keras, etc.) to implement specific traditional machine learning analyses.
Write software components or scripts under the supervision of a senior team member.

public_objective_groups.title: Trustworthy AI
public_objective_groups.description: Creation and assessment of ethical, energy-conscious, and reliable artificial intelligence systems capable of interpreting and integrating various forms of data, ensuring that they're designed and applied in a manner that's transparent, fair, and verifiable.
objectives: Describe the ethical principles of trustworthy AI.
Describe the balance between data privacy and the importance of data consent.
Describe how to use NVIDIA and other technologies to improve AI trustworthiness.
Describe how to minimize bias in AI systems.
